what: Writes Wisp code may make to power, clock or trim registers that no Renode model acts on (tests/boot/strict.py). Each entry is one register and one value ("*" only where the value is a read-modify-write of reset-dependent state), names what stock 2.4.0.24 does with the same register at the same point, and needs review like code. Since W25 (docs/wisp/rung4.md, 'The start-up writes, stock against native-0/native-1'): native-1's HAL start-up, which makes stock's calls with stock's values. The SIMO buck block (MCUCTRL.VRCTRL, SIMOBUCK0/15, PWRCTRL.VRCTRL) is not listed: WispPwrctrl now answers VRSTATUS.SIMOBUCKST as silicon does after the bootloader, so the HAL skips it as stock does; a write there still fails a case. Wisp Boot and stage-0 make none of these writes.

entries.reason: ERR027: the BORSTAT bit cleared by read-modify-write, so the value is whatever the reset left minus bit 2. Stock does the same at 0x4951EC, the bootloader at 0x41C4D0. native-1 reads STAT before it.
bits 3:0 cleared (two RMW) in am_hal_pwrctrl_low_power_init (native-1: src/soc/wisp_soc_init.c, stock's own first start-up call); stock 0x495212/0x49521A.
|= 1 in am_hal_pwrctrl_low_power_init (native-1: src/soc/wisp_soc_init.c, stock's own first start-up call); stock 0x495230.

set and cleared around the memory configuration (am_hal_pwrctrl_mcu_memory_config) in am_hal_pwrctrl_low_power_init (native-1: src/soc/wisp_soc_init.c, stock's own first start-up call); stock calls the same at 0x4952C4 with the same defaults (ITCM 256K/DTCM 512K, NVM0+1).
